items.headline: Tesla ships FSD V15, and the feed spends the night watching its new Reality View
items.summary: Tesla's V15 release notes describe a rebuilt end-to-end network: a vision encoder shared by FSD, Robotaxi and Optimus, trained on internet video, that they say cuts the critical intervention rate 25x, and a single "Reality View" visualization that uses less total compute. @elonmusk called it "a banger release" and clarified overnight that "we mean 25 times," not 25%. Tesla AI's @aelluswamy said the view is "produced end-to-end, pixels-in-pixels-out," and owners spent the night posting clips of it rendering Toronto streetcars and a historic church.
items.short: A new driving network and a generated, video-game-like view of the road; the safety claim is Tesla's own.

items.headline: Musk: next year's AI cash crunch will be "nuts"
items.summary: "Getting this amount of compute turned on, cooled and working reliably is incredibly hard," @elonmusk wrote Saturday; even a few months' lag between paying for compute and earning on it "will mean hundreds of billions of incremental dollars just for working capital. Where will that come from?" Skeptics like @rdd147 read it as a call against the neoclouds; @SMASIMHO answered with Nebius's Roman Chernin: "If demand is there, the working capital problem can be solved."
items.short: A working-capital warning for the AI build-out, and the neocloud debate it restarted.

items.headline: Anthropic now holds $237 billion in cash after its IPO
items.summary: @KobeissiLetter tallied Anthropic's cash and equivalents at a record $237 billion after an IPO that raised $81 billion plus a $26 billion private placement: about 8 times Nvidia's cash and more than Alphabet, Amazon, SpaceX and Apple combined (Berkshire holds $377 billion). The same account noted that AI-related investment added 1.27 points to US GDP growth in the first three quarters, about 65% of the total.
items.short: A war chest bigger than four megacaps combined, as AI spending carries the economy.

items.headline: Buy the dip or wait? The feed splits after the Nasdaq's 20% fall
items.summary: @ren_stocks pointed out that the Nasdaq 100 is down 20% from its October peak and the S&P 500 12% with "no lockdown, no bank failure, no earnings collapse." @DeepValueBagger is not buying yet: unwinds take three to six months, and he is watching the Nvidia SEC inquiry, a Dec. 1 hearing for Jensen Huang and a price base forming. @danielisdizzy relayed Tom Lee's case for a fast bear market and a faster recovery, citing Cisco in 1997.

items.author: Paul Millerd
items.text:
how to (start) writing a book

1. open a document in word or google docs, or build your own document editor
2. format it in a way you like, build a dynamic table of contents.
3. Start filling out a rough high level structure, take material you already have and paste it in the document
4. write for a month without worrying about title, how to publish it, publishing deals, proposals etc..
5. at the end of the month listen to your gut about what the next step is

this is all you need to do.  don't get stuck in the stories about doing a book or the identity of being an "aspiring author" …

items.author: Gavin Baker
items.text:
Basically, approved datacenter sales inside China, workstation/gaming GPU sales inside China and GPUs rented to Chinese labs from various clouds in SE Asia, Europe and America are all different.

Investors understood all of this. https://t.co/iHTi10RgD8

quoted.author: Gavin Baker
quoted.text:
I don’t know a single investor who feels misled. And I know almost all of the large ones personally.

Jensen consistently said beginning in mid/late 2025 that “we are assuming/forecasting China datacenter sales to be zero” and then on the calls Colette would note that approved China datacenter sales were sub 1% of revenue. No one cares abt that differential (forecasting zero vs. sub 1%). Most recent disclosure of $2.4b was more precise but directionally consistent at 2% of quarterly revenue. Also gaming and workstation GPUs are not datacenter GPUs.

And investors understood that SE Asian, European and US clouds/hyperscalers were renting GPUs to Chinese labs from all of those geographies (ie American hyperscalers were renting GPUs to Chinese labs from their SE Asian, European and American availability zones). Which is obviously the most pro-national security policy of all as can literally turn them off in any conflict. This would dramatically curtail China’s ability to use AI (need inference capacity) overnight. This gave America arguably more leverage over China than they had over us through rare earths. And our leverage would have grown every year while theirs shrank.

Now Alibaba is saying that Huawei will be at parity (tho way less power efficient but China has loads of power) in a year. Those Huawei systems will undoubtedly make their way to Russia, North Korea and Iran and endanger America due to well-intentioned China Hawks in DC and the media.

Our old policy guaranteed America would always be ahead. New course much riskier imo.

Btw have enjoyed your writing over the years.

items.author: Daniel
items.text:
$CRWV is now trading below its March 2025 IPO price of $40.

Yesterday, the stock closed at $39.51, down 80% from its all-time high.

Its market cap is now just $21B.

Management expects to exit 2026 with an annualized revenue run rate of $21B.

CoreWeave has a $132.5B backlog, but more importantly, its financial profile is improving.

Look at how net interest expenses are evolving as a percentage of revenue:

• Q1 2026: 25.8%
• Q2 2026: 24.9%
• Q3 2026: 23.1%

Over those six months, revenue increased 76%, while net interest expenses increased just 58%.

CoreWeave is growing its business faster than its financing burden.

And contrary to the market narrative, its cost of debt is declining.

During the Q3 earnings call, CEO Michael Intrator stated:

“At the end of Q3, our weighted average cost of debt across our entire business was 7.9%, down 250 basis points year-over-year.”

CoreWeave is growing rapidly, improving its financial position, and reducing its average cost of debt.

Yet its stock is trading below its IPO price from nearly two years ago.

Nothing justifies an 80% collapse from its highs while the underlying business continues to strengthen.

items.title: Why Nebius's power curve matters more than its size
items.author: Melvin
items.summary: A walk through one forecast chart: Nebius's active power growing from 170 MW in 2025 to about 5 GW by 2033, with revenue per megawatt projected to rise from $3.2 million to $14.9 million by 2029, passing CoreWeave's projected peak. The useful idea is the framing: power sets how many GPUs you can run, but revenue per megawatt says whether customers fill them. It is a bull case built on a forecast, worth rereading against this week's neocloud selloff.

items.title: Four Cards
items.rule: If a person is drinking beer, they must be over 21.
items.explanation: Drinking beer could hide something that breaks the rule; Age 17 breaks it if the other side turns out to be Drinking beer. Age 25 can't break it (the rule never says only those cards have it), and Drinking soda isn't covered by the rule at all. Most people pick the card that matches the rule's second half instead of the one that could falsify it. Most people get this version right and the letters-and-numbers version wrong, though the logic is identical.

across.clue: Joyful religious song celebrating the birth of Christ
A message that departs from the main subject
The seat within a bishop's diocese where his cathedral is located

down.clue: A relation that provides the foundation for something
An elaborate or deceitful scheme contrived to deceive or evade
The side of something that is sheltered from the wind

Not math specific, but a society which moves in the direction of not correctly and fairly assigning credit and ownership of what Great Individuals achieve is doomed. 

The foundation of modern western civilization was built on radical innovations around property rights. We want those with the capacity to do and invent and discover to defensibly own that which they create so they can be motivated to create more of it for us. Credit & recognition is required.
